text:
maria: ran a short Nsight capture of the flaky inference job — timeline looks like memcpy bursts interleaving with long CPU scheduling gaps. suspect KV cache refills triggering lots of host->device copies :thinking:

maria: capture: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt,nvtx --output=runA --duration=12 --sample=none ./bin/serve --config conf/prod.yaml`

devin: can you paste the timeline screenshot or a small ascii summary? curious which streams show overlap.

maria: pasted quick ascii:
```
Time -> |----|----|----|----|----|\nStream 0: [kernel:fused_attn][idle][kernel:band_matmul][idle]
Stream 2: [memcpy H2D big chunk][memcpy H2D small][idle]
CPU    : [worker sched gap 20ms][kv-serializer 80%][worker runs]
```

maria: interesting bits: memcpy bursts (~3.2–4ms each) frequently precede tiny kernels (~0.2–0.6ms). kernels don't batch up because host only sends small jobs.

olga: that sounds like batching heuristic is emitting small batches too eagerly. what's batcher.max_delay_ms right now?

maria: 2ms in prod for low-latency tier. also saw repeated `kv_cache_load` kernel calls — each TTL-miss causes host to pull and memcpy a slot.

raj: do you have kernel names/launch counts? maybe kernel selection picks many small kernels instead of a fused path.

maria: yes: `fused_attention_v2` launches 1200 calls, avg 0.45ms; `band_matmul` 900 calls, avg 2.3ms; `kv_cache_load` 2400 mem ops (small) causing host->device memcpy churn.

ben: perf-bot flagged a CPU-side hotspot at the same time — `kv-serializer` thread doing JSON marshalling with lock contention, causing scheduling gaps on the worker threads :eyes:

perf-bot: generated flamegraph -> https://perf.local/runs/1776212345/flame.html (hot: kv-serializer::serialize, http_poller::poll)

devin: two likely causes then: (A) batching heuristic too aggressive -> many small host transfers, (B) KV cache eviction pattern causing synchronous loads. both cause memcpy to appear on critical path.

olga: quick mitigations?

maria: try 1) increase batcher.max_delay_ms to 6ms for this model (trade latency for throughput), 2) enable pinned host buffers for prefetch to reduce memcpy stall, 3) change KV cache eviction policy: prefetch hot keys into GPU pool, 4) adjust kernel selector to prefer `fused_attention_big_launch` when seq_len>128 to reduce kernel count.

raj: any quick repro to validate? maybe run a focused profile that filters only CUDA memcpy and our kernels: `nsys stats runA.qdrep --report=nvtx --format=timeline` and `nsys profile --trace=cuda --output=stepA --stop-at-call 200 ./bin/serve --batch-size=...`

maria: I also captured CPU scheduling markers with `--trace=osrt` and added `NVTX` spans around batcher hold. NVTX showed huge white gaps (no GPU work) while user threads were blocked on a mutex in kv-serializer.

ben: curious: are memcpys happening on default stream causing implicit syncs? if H2D is on a different stream but host thread waits on completion, that forces serial behavior. check if code uses `cudaMemcpy` vs `cudaMemcpyAsync` with pinned memory.

maria: grep: we still have `cudaMemcpy` in `kv_store.cc` codepath for fallback. that's on the TODO list. switching to `cudaMemcpyAsync` + pinned host buffer should allow overlap.

devin: plan: 1) repro with nvtx+osrt capture and smaller duration (~10s) to validate overlap after changing to async+pin, 2) flip batcher.max_delay to 6ms for canary, 3) instrument kv cache prefetch counters and eviction TTL to watch misses. I'll make a canary branch.

olga: add a quick unit test that simulates hot key thrash pattern to reproduce eviction-induced memcpys. will help prevent regression.

maria: also a note on kernel selection: the trace shows multiple small kernels because we fallback to non-fused matmul when sequence chunking < 32. maybe increase chunk threshold so we use fused kernels more often; that reduced kernel launches in previous experiment.

raj: sounds good. if this reduces memcpy frequency and CPU gaps go away, we can roll to staging. otherwise we may need to look at moving kv cache metadata to shared GPU-resident table (bigger change).

ben: i'll add a perf alert that fires when memcpy time / total GPU time > 0.25 for sustained 10s — should catch regressions earlier. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks everyone — I'll push the async memcpy + pinned buffer patch and post a follow-up capture in this thread once I have results.

devin: great, @maria please drop the new capture output link here.

maria: will do — targeting a canary later today. :rocket:
